content.text:
IPv6 literal brackets in link destinations are no longer percent-encoded. `[visit](http://[2001:db8::1]/)` now renders as `<a href="http://[2001:db8::1]/">`.

The cause was in `normalizeLink` in `src/markdownit.ts`. It ran the whole URL through `mdurl.encode`, which encodes `[` and `]` everywhere, including around an IPv6 host. After encoding, it now puts the literal brackets back around the host when the hostname contains a colon. Brackets elsewhere in the URL are still encoded: `/a[b]` still comes out as `/a%5Bb%5D`.

I rebuilt and checked it by hand: an inline link and an autolink (`<http://[::1]:80/x>`) both keep their brackets. All 300 tests in `test/markdown-it` pass. I didn't add a regression test, and I didn't run the other test suites (`test:cmspec`, `test:build`), lint or type-check.
